title: the colour-space compaction loop guards on j while reading j + 1, so it reads one element past the format array
object: formats->formats, one av_malloc_array(count, sizeof(int)) built by MAKE_FORMAT_LIST at libavfilter/formats.c:429
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the buffer is alive throughout. This corpus's rows are spatial by construction.
shape: the shift loop's guard is `j < nb_formats` while its body reads `formats[j + 1]`, so the last iteration reads index nb_formats
allocator_layer: the platform allocator itself: one direct allocation, no inner layer. Nothing sub-allocated the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row is NOT NESTED. Recorded explicitly because the tally is per corpus and case.json carries no nested field.
fidelity:
real allocator, model consumer. Reduced: `sws_test_colorspace` is replaced by "the first element fails", which is the
arrangement that makes the shift loop run its full length and so reach the last index; the formats are
plain ints. The out-of-bounds read is probed one byte wide at the first byte past the array, which is
the narrowest possible crossing of that bound.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source, not from ancestry: n9.0.1:libavfilter/vf_scale.c contains the FIXED form (1 occurrence) and the pre-fix form 0 times. Two-sided, so the probe is known to fire; ancestry was deliberately not used, having called backported fixes live before. A fix-reversal: the pre-fix consumer shape is reconstructed against the shipped allocator, the convention at ../../memcached/allocator-repros/README.md:132-135.
distinguishing: the only row here where upstream states the crossed value is DISCARDED, so `damage` is 0 on both arms and the crossing alone is the finding. That is the distinction a bounds machine makes and a consequence-based test cannot: the fix was taken for the read, not for its effect.

spatial.oracle: PREDICTED: FAULTS at the labelled probe. The crossing leaves the allocation the platform allocator handed out, which per-object bounds enforce. NOT YET MEASURED: this corpus has no capstone-domain runner, as is also true of the two sibling plain-heap corpora. WHY THE PLATFORM ALLOCATOR. These cases call the platform's calloc, not the buffer-pool port's av_malloc. That port's av_malloc (ports/ffmpeg/buffer-pool/src/shared/metadata-allocator.c:26) is a bump/freelist carve out of ONE arena returning a raw interior pointer, and it rounds every request up to 64 bytes; __builtin_capstone_cap_shrink appears only in src/capstone-domain/payload-capabilities.c:57, on pool PAYLOAD blocks. Routing these cases through it would leave no per-allocation bound to cross AND would absorb every small crossing in the round-up, so the reading would be about the arena, not the defect.

sublet.oracle: PREDICTED: faults, identically to the spatial arm. Sublet is revocation and has nothing to fire on while the buffer is alive; the catch is the inherited per-object bound. NOT YET MEASURED.

poisoncap-spatial.oracle: PREDICTED and UNMEASURABLE HERE: faults. Mode 0 bounds each allocation and the crossing leaves one. Unmeasurable on this host, checked rather than assumed: ports/common/cmake/toolchains/cheribsd.cmake:4-9 FATAL_ERRORs without CHERI_SDK and CHERI_SYSROOT.

poisoncap-protected.oracle: PREDICTED and UNMEASURABLE HERE: faults, for the mode-0 reason.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: PREDICTED, NOT MEASURED: CAUGHT at the labelled probe. THE PREDICTION IS CONDITIONAL AND THE CONDITION IS THE POINT. CheriBSD's malloc bounds a capability to the allocator's USABLE SIZE, not to the request -- measured in-guest on this host 2026-10-06: calloc(1,1) and calloc(1,9) both return length 16, calloc(1,17) returns 32, calloc(1,8192) returns exactly 8192. So a crossing is caught only when it leaves the USABLE allocation. This case requests 24 bytes and crosses the first byte past the end, which is past a 24-byte request; 24 is not a size-class boundary, so the usable size must be read in-guest before this is believed. memcached/plain-heap-repros/00 predicted a catch on the same argument and was REFUTED by exactly this mechanism, so the size is recorded here rather than assumed away. The reading must be taken in-guest for THIS request size and allocation call -- the calloc table above is not transferable to a differently-aligned request.

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED two-sided 2026-10-06, 20261006-native-plain-heap/: ASan REPORTS, and upstream predicted exactly that: its commit message says the excess element 'was never actually used, but it still triggers ASAN'. The FIXED arm is silent and exits 0, so the detector is shown to separate the arms rather than merely to fire. The runner keys on heap-buffer-overflow, never on the string 'AddressSanitizer' -- LeakSanitizer's summary contains that string and would make a leak read as a bounds detection. Built -O0, so a discarded out-of-bounds read is not optimised away.

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm reaches touched=6 at cap=6, crossed=1; the fixed arm touched=5, crossed=0. ASan two-sided: buggy REPORTS, fixed silent.
